findings.title: Entries tab can fail with an unhandled lookup error after a job is deleted

evidence.detail: The entries and jobs streams are combined and each entry is matched to its job with jobs.firstWhere(...) and no orElse. If the jobs snapshot arrives before the entries snapshot reflects a deletion, or an entry is orphaned, this throws a StateError and the whole Entries tab falls back to 'Can't load items right now'.
deleteJob removes the entries one at a time and then the job, so there is a window where the two streams disagree. A reviewer who swipes away a job and then opens the Entries tab can hit this.

fix.recipe: In _entriesJobsCombiner skip entries whose job is missing (use where/firstWhereOrNull) instead of throwing. Delete a job and its entries in one Firestore batch. Add a unit test with an orphaned entry.

findings.guideline: iOS 2.1 App Completeness; iOS 2.3 Accurate Metadata
findings.title: Hourly rate accepts whole numbers only, and invalid input silently becomes 0 so pay disappears

evidence.detail: The rate field uses decimal: false and has no validator. Typing 12.50 or leaving the field empty is parsed with int.tryParse(...) ?? 0 (line 127) and saved as 0 with no message.
Pay is only shown when ratePerHour > 0. A job saved with a silently dropped rate shows no pay anywhere, although the listing sells the app as tracking pay.
The listing subtitle is 'Track jobs, entries and pay'. A reviewer testing with a typical rate such as 12.50 sees pay vanish or the value change with no explanation.

fix.recipe: Add a validator that rejects empty or non-numeric rates, or allow decimals. Store the rate as a double or as minor units and update Job.fromMap, which currently casts to int. Add a widget test for 12.50 and for an empty field.

findings.title: Description promises hours and pay per job, but no per-job total exists

evidence.detail: The iOS description says the user can 'see how many hours and how much pay each job adds up to'.
The Jobs list tile shows only the job name and a chevron. It has no hours or pay total.
The Entries tab shows one overall total plus per-day, per-job rows. The user has to add the days up by hand to get a total for one job.

fix.recipe: Either show a lifetime hours and pay total on the job entries screen and the job tile, or reword the iOS description to 'see hours and pay per day and per job' so it matches what the Entries tab shows.

findings.guideline: iOS 2.1 App Completeness; iOS 5.1.1(v) data control
findings.title: Swiping a job away deletes it and all its entries at once, with no confirmation or undo

evidence.detail: onDismissed calls deleteJob immediately, and the only cue is a plain red background. Nothing says that the job's time entries go too.
deleteJob permanently deletes every entry of the job before deleting the job. A stray swipe wipes the user's work, and a network failure partway leaves a half-deleted job.

fix.recipe: Use Dismissible.confirmDismiss with an alert that names the entries being deleted, or show a SnackBar with Undo. Commit the delete as a single Firestore batch.

findings.guideline: iOS 5.1.1(v) Account Deletion; iOS 2.1 App Completeness
findings.title: Anonymous users get no warning before sign-out, and their account deletion cannot re-authenticate

evidence.detail: SignOutButton signs out immediately. An anonymous user's account and data can never be recovered afterwards, as the support page says. The profile screen only shows 'Signed in anonymously' (line 32) and gives no warning or upgrade path.

If Firebase asks for a recent login, the re-authentication dialog is built from authProviders, which holds only EmailAuthProvider (auth_providers.dart line 14). An anonymous user has no email or password to enter, so deletion cannot finish. The review notes (store/review_notes.yaml) point reviewers at this anonymous path to test deletion.
Anonymous sign-in is offered as an equal choice on the sign-in screen with no mention that the data is tied to this device session.

fix.recipe: Before sign-out for an anonymous user, show a confirmation that the data will be lost. For anonymous users skip the email re-auth dialog: tell them to delete from a fresh session, or link the account to an email first. Offer 'Create account' to link the credential.
